newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: WTO to rule on US import embargo on shrimp.
newsitem.headline: WTO to rule on US import embargo on shrimp.

text.p: The World Trade Organisation (WTO) established a neutral panel to rule on complaints by three Asian countries against a partial U.S. embargo on imports of shrimp and shrimp products, a WTO spokesman said.
Thailand, Malaysia and Pakistan complained that the U.S. ban violates free trading rules, arguing that it amounted to a bid to apply domestic environmental laws outside its borders.
Thailand took the floor at WTO's Dispute Settlement Body to say that the problem was the U.S. law was extraterritorial, according to trade sources at the closed-door talks in Geneva.
The U.S. ban, affecting hundreds of millions of dollars in trade, is a public law amending the 1973 Endangered Species Act.

It was implemented in mid-1996 against countries judged by Washington to be using fishing methods that also entrap sea turtles -- a species internationally recognised as being in danger of extinction.
Pakistan complained that its shrimp exports had been adversely effected by the embargo despite attempts to resolve the row during consultations last November.

The U.S. delegation took the floor to say that its law had only a small efffect on trade between the United States and Pakistan but did not oppose a consolidated panel being set up to consider the complaint by all three Asian countries.

The European Community, India, Guatemala, Japan, Sri Lanka, Nigeria, the Philippines, Singapore, Australia, Colombia, Hong Kong and Mexico reserved their rights as third parties to the dispute, according to trade sources.
